brackets.section: Announcement 2024-03, schedules "effective tax year 2025"; under Tax Year 2026 it says the brackets are the same as in tax year 2025
brackets.note: All three schedules read from the announcement. The brackets reproduce its printed top-bracket amounts ($25,966 single, $51,932 joint, $38,949 head of household). The 2026 Booklet A annual withholding rates use the same thresholds. Tax Foundation (single, joint) and PolicyEngine (all three) agree. The schedule changes again in 2027.

earnedIncomeCredit.note: "forty per cent of the federal earned income tax credit allowed and properly claimed", refundable. The 40% is from Act 163 of 2023, which is repealed on December 31, 2027, after which the credit is 20%.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: Hawaii earned income tax credit

standardDeduction.note: Act 46 raised the amounts for 2026. Tax Foundation shows $4,400 single and $8,800 joint, which are the 2024 and 2025 amounts, so its row is stale. The state announcement wins. PolicyEngine agrees with the 2026 amounts.

personalExemption.section: N-11 instructions, line 25 exemptions; Booklet A appendix, value of each regular withholding allowance
personalExemption.note: $1,144 per exemption, read in the 2025 N-11 instructions. The 2026 return instructions are not out, but the 2026 Booklet A sets each withholding allowance at $1,144 and Tax Foundation's 2026 table lists the same. Filers 65 or older get a second exemption, which is not modeled.

rules.note: Local tax flag is from Tax Foundation footnote (a), which does not list Hawaii. Payroll flag read in the DLIR 2026 notice: employers may withhold half the premium cost, no more than 0.5% of weekly wages and no more than $7.50 a week. Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions.
notes: Employers may withhold half the temporary disability insurance premium from wages, no more than 0.5% of weekly pay or $7.50 a week. Not included.
Not modeled: additional $1,144 exemption for a filer or spouse aged 65 or older, and the larger disability exemption taken in place of the regular ones.
Not modeled: the alternative tax on capital gains, the food/excise tax credit and the low-income household renters credit.
maintainerNotes: Employers may withhold part of the temporary disability insurance premium from wages. From general knowledge, the employee share is capped at 0.5% of weekly wages up to a maximum. Needs checking.
Check whether Hawaii allows the federal overtime and tip deductions. Hawaii does not conform to federal changes automatically.
Announcement 2024-03 widens the brackets again for 2027 and raises the standard deduction again for 2028. PolicyEngine also records a 13% top bracket from 2027 under Act 24 of 2026. Recheck for 2027.
